subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a core browser private-network SSRF approval policy, and what first-phase security contract should it expose?
rationale: The request changes browser egress semantics, public config, and possibly user approval UI/CLI state; automation cannot safely choose those security and product tradeoffs.

options.title: Approve staged browser policy
options.body: Start with a narrow browser-owned allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local semantics, then add interactive confirmation only after prompt, timeout, rate-limit, redirect, and session-state UX is specified.

options.title: Keep current strict knobs
options.body: Leave the current strict deny, broad dangerous opt-in, and hostname exception model in place and document why interactive private-network grants are unsupported.

options.title: Fold into broader egress design
options.body: Resolve this together with browser denylist and generic egress-policy work before adding browser-specific SSRF config.

recommendation.title: Approve staged browser policy
recommendation.body: Start with a narrow browser-owned allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local semantics, then add interactive confirmation only after prompt, timeout, rate-limit, redirect, and session-state UX is specified.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across browser config/security and adjacent SSRF policy decisions.
